title: Pathwidth and vertex separation

problem.name: Pathwidth
problem.statement_latex:
Minimize $\max_i|B_i|-1$ over path decompositions: bags $B_1,\ldots,B_r$ cover all vertices and edges, and each vertex occurs in consecutive bags. Equivalently, minimize over vertex orders the largest number of already placed vertices with a neighbor still unplaced. Pathwidth captures the live frontier in linear processing and memory allocation.
The quantum algorithm is measured in QRAM time and classical ordering algorithms in RAM operations.

quantum.details_latex: The vertex-separation objective admits a subset recurrence: each state records an already placed prefix and its boundary. Partial preprocessing and quantum minimum finding optimize the largest boundary along a full ordering, using exponential coherent storage.

classical.headline_latex: $O^*(1.89^n)$, Kitsunai et al. directed-pathwidth algorithm applied to an undirected graph.
classical.details_latex: Replace each edge by its two opposite arcs; this preserves the relevant vertex-separation objective. The algorithm exploits structural restrictions on orderings and improves the generic $O^*(2^n)$ subset recurrence. Its exponential parameter remains the original number of vertices.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup through a smaller exponential constant relative to the $1.89^n$ classical bound. The quantum acceleration comes from recursive minimum finding and amplitude amplification.

hardware.description_latex: The active subset, boundary-count and reconstruction registers use polynomially many logical qubits. Exponential QRAM and long coherent recursive searches dominate useful-instance requirements.
